_doc: Every image in samples/ must have an entry here — tests/test_localize.py fails on an
undocumented file. That is deliberate: the corpus is only worth anything if what each
screenshot is meant to prove is written down.
capture — 'crop' or 'fullscreen'. Crops have no screen geometry to anchor to; full-screen
shots carry the game's own chrome around the board and prove the localizer finds
the scoreboard inside a much larger frame.
localizes — false means the localizer is expected to refuse this image today. The reason is
asserted in the tests, so if it ever starts succeeding, that gets noticed.
atlas_source — true means the digit atlas is cut from this image's ground truth. Anything
with ground truth and atlas_source false is a held-out set, and is where the
accuracy numbers that mean anything come from. It defaults to false on purpose:
adding a new expected.json must never silently absorb the validation set into

images.notes: Ground truth, and the image the digit atlas is cut from. Every row has a nameplate; four have title lines.
One blue row has no nameplate.
Two rows carry no title line.
Three rows have no nameplate at all. Filename contains a space, which is why the loader decodes from bytes rather than handing a path to cv2.imread.

Native full-screen capture with the game's FPS counter, chat box and ESC prompt around the board. Widest board in the corpus. One red row has no nameplate. Blue is 3 tank / 1 damage / 2 support — Open Queue, so role composition is not fixed. Held out from the atlas: this is the validation set.
Post-match SUMMARY/TEAMS/PERSONAL screen, full-screen. Three rows have no nameplate.
As above at a different resolution. One blue row has no nameplate.

notes: The only in-game Tab shot in the corpus, and the only ultrawide (2.5:1). Carries the
things an endgame report cannot: the hero ban row, 'CONTROL | ANTARCTIC PENINSULA',
the match clock, and the rank range. app/extract/tab.py localizes all four; every
chrome threshold in that module is fitted to this one screenshot.
`localizes: false` is about the *endgame* localizer, which must keep refusing it.
It refuses on the column signature: both boards print E A D DMG H MIT, but the Tab
board packs them left to reserve its right edge for the mute buttons, so MIT lands
74 canonical units early where the endgame corpus agrees within 1.6.
An earlier note here blamed the refusal on the blue block overrunning the header by
~467 units. That was wrong. The Tab board aligns with its header strip as tightly as
any endgame report; the overrun was Junker Queen's blue hair in the hero panel, which
shares the block's scanlines and was being swallowed by a min-to-max column extent.
